serial.plan_and_ownership: Handled all five layers sequentially in the main trajectory, using todos and local commits rather than child ownership.
serial.implementation: Implemented WiFi locally and explicitly chose any association state change as the handover count, producing coverage of 82.0.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all experiment modules into run.sh and produced per-requirement patches in the final workspace.
serial.verification: Ran run.sh with all 25 output lines and an API conformance check; the local check passed after setting PYTHONPATH.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Same task prompt required all five layers and pointed to requirements and module output tests as source of truth.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same task prompt and requirement set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material prompt difference; the divergence came from the parallel WiFi child result lifecycle and differing WiFi interpretation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent used AgentSwarm with five total subagent ids in the parallel protocol record and delegated the remaining layers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled Agent and AgentSwarm and recorded zero subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split ownership across child actors, while serial kept all implementation and verification decisions in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The WiFi child received a detailed layer brief including the requirement file, output keys, mobility parameters, and handover wording.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept the WiFi ambiguity in its own context and reasoned about whether handover should count any association change.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important difference was not missing initial context, but whether the completed WiFi result's ambiguous assumption was adjudicated before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel WiFi counted only AP-to-AP transitions and computed coverage from that child trace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial WiFi counted any association-state change and produced coverage from its local trace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This implementation choice yielded parallel 3/71.60 versus serial 18/82.0 for the two WiFi mobility metrics.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The WiFi child completed and returned concrete values and an explicit AP-to-AP handover decision to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run's WiFi decision and output remained in the same main trajectory rather than crossing a child result boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a completed child handoff that needed parent adjudication; serial had no handoff boundary for that decision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent integrated all child modules into a shared workspace and committed each requirement with run.sh updates.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run built and committed all layers directly in the single main workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision explains the WiFi gap; both runs produced an assembled run.sh, but with different WiFi values.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reran module outputs showing the bad WiFi values, then closed with counts of lines and key-value formatting.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran run.sh, saw WiFi 18/82.0, and then got API conformance checks passing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel final verification did not substantively challenge the WiFi child values; serial's local path at least found the coverage behavior that matched the official tolerance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used substantially more requests, tools, and six wire files, but completed before timeout and closed after the shallow check.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one wire file with fewer requests and tools and also completed before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no timeout or budget-exhaustion label; the closure difference is that the parallel parent accepted the child result without resolving the WiFi metric assumptions.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed status.json evaluations failed. The concrete difference is inside the WiFi metrics: parallel failed both handover and coverage after accepting the child WiFi result, while serial failed handover but passed coverage after a different local handover/coverage implementation.
parallel_contributors: Completed WiFi child result with 3 handovers and 71.60 coverage was accepted without substantive parent adjudication.
Final parallel verification counted output lines and key-value separators rather than checking the questionable WiFi values.
serial_contributors: Serial kept the WiFi ambiguity in one local reasoning path and chose to count any association-state change.
Serial run.sh printed WIFI_COVERAGE_PCT 82.0, which the official status records as passing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two WiFi implementations used different handover semantics and mobility trace handling.
Both implementations still missed the hidden handover target, so neither solution passed overall.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributors for the WiFi quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a pass/fail outcome difference.
